newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Israel's Levy says Brussels meet did further peace.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Levy says Brussels meet did further peace.

text.p: Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy said on Wednesday a meeting he had with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat did take forward the stalled Middle East peace process.
"If we want to be realistic, this meeting in Brussels gave new impetus to the talks," Levy said after meeting Belgian Foreign Minister Eric Derycke.
Earlier on Wednesday, Arafat dampened optimistic statements after his meeting with Levy on Tuesday on the margins of a European Union foreign ministers meeting, saying nothing had been achieved.
By contrast, Levy was very upbeat. "We have every reason to be optimistic. We have taken a step forward. It is of great importance in Israel, for the Palestinians, for the world as a whole," he said.
However, Levy rejected the idea of a freeze on a house building project in Arab east Jerusalem that has sent the Israel/PLO peace talks sliding into crisis since April.
"We made no pre-conditions (to a resumption of the peace talks) yesterday," Levy said, adding that he hoped for further progress in coming days.
